name: Sri Lanka
title: Holidays in Sri Lanka
intro: Leopards, elephants, a famous train ride and golden beaches on one small island. Here's what Sri Lanka is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 4½ to 5½ hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: December to March is best for the south and west coasts and the hill country. May to September is the time for the east coast, while the south-west has its monsoon. October and November are wet across much of the island.

things.name: Yala National Park
things.blurb: Jeep safaris with one of the world's best chances of seeing a leopard.

things.name: Sigiriya
things.blurb: Climb about 1,200 steps up an ancient rock fortress. Go early, before the heat.

things.name: Kandy to Ella train
things.blurb: A slow, famous ride through tea plantations. Book seats ahead.

things.name: Galle Fort
things.blurb: A walled old town by the sea, with cafés and ramparts to walk.

things.name: Udawalawe
things.blurb: Herds of elephants on a jeep safari, almost guaranteed.

things.name: Whale watching
things.blurb: Blue whales off Mirissa, from November to April.

faqs.question: Is Sri Lanka good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's friendly and good value, and you can see wildlife, hills and beaches in two weeks. Hiring a car and driver is the easiest way to get around.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Twelve to fourteen nights covers the Cultural Triangle, the hill country, a safari and the beach.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: British passport holders need an ETA, applied for online before you travel. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Which beaches are best for children?
faqs.answer: Sheltered bays such as Unawatuna and Hiriketiya on the south coast in winter, and Pasikudah on the east coast in summer. Many beaches have strong currents, so check before swimming.
